text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London closed higher on continued fund and industry buying with benchmark July finishing at the highest level since mid-March.

Traders said further gains are on the cards as roasters still have much price-fixing to do. May and July ended $27 higher at $1,720 and $1,780 per tonne respectively. Traders said the upward momentum in London was also speeded by lack of aggressive origin offers.
Indonesian sellers were sidelined either because of a local holiday in the country or they are expecting much higher levels, it was said.

Arabica futures in New York ended mostly higher in moderate dealings bolstered by speculative buying amid news of a strike by port workers at Brazil's key port of Santos. The port worker strike, which only affected public terminals sparked enough buying to trigger technical buy-stops above 213.50 cents/lb basis July.

Santos is Brazil's key coffee loading port, accounting for just under 1 mn bags of the 1.2 mn bags covered so far by bills of lading for April shipment. The work stoppage, protesting delayed payment of port workers' full April salary, will continue until the workers receive written confirmation that the port authority has paid the remaining salary. July finished 5.50 cents/lb higher at 216.90 cents/lb, while September added 3.15 cents/lb to close at 194.50 cents/lb.

After the close on Thursday the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks increased by 750 bags which could put pressure on prices on Friday. If more coffee shows up at the exchange for certification and the Brazilian strike is resolved quickly some traders said July may try to test key technical support at 209.00 cents/lb. However, the increase in certified coffee stocks is only marginal and inventories remain extremely low.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks rose by 750 60-kg bags on May 7 to 25,419 bags the previous day but down on the 27,669 bags recorded on May 5. There were 3,998 bags pending grading in New York, 9,995 bags in New Orleans and 3,750 bags in Miami.

BRAZIL - The Brazilian government sold 128,005 bags, or 63.97 per cent of the 200,090 60-kg bags of coffee stocks offered to all segments of the coffee sector in its auction on May 7. Total revenue for the government was just over 18.5 mn reais ($17.45 mn).

FRANCE - France imported 614,000 bags of coffee in January 1997, 15 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 7.2 per cent to 6.696 mn bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January 1997 were Uganda (61,300 vs 34,000 bags), Brazil (109,400 vs 70,900 bags) and Colombia (50,300 vs 61,700 bags). The country exported 103,700 bags of coffee in January 1997, 48 per cent more than was shipped the same month the previous year. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 10 per cent to 1.186 mn bags.

SINGAPORE - Singapore imported 1.417 mn bags of coffee in calendar year 1996, 26 per cent less than was imported the previous year. The main supplier of green coffee in 1996 was Vietnam with 200,200 bags against 514,800 bags the previous year. Exports in 1996 reached 1.349 mn bags, 28 per cent less than was exported in 1995.

IRELAND - Ireland imported 111,200 bags of coffee in January/November 1996, 4 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 15 per cent to 114,900 bags. The country imports most of its coffee in the form of solubles from the United Kingdom.
